hero.title: SFDA Medical Device Registration & MDMA Services in Saudi Arabia
hero.subtitle: Plan, prepare and manage your Saudi market-entry pathway with focused support for MDMA readiness, technical documentation and GHAD lifecycle requirements.
hero.whatsappCta: Talk to our Saudi team on WhatsApp

audience.title: A clearer starting point for Saudi market access
audience.body: Whether you are planning a first entry, assessing an existing dossier, or preparing a new device variant, we help organise the regulatory work before the submission stage.

items.title: New to Saudi Arabia
items.text: Understand the initial pathway, local coordination requirements and the information that should be assembled first.

items.title: Working from existing approvals
items.text: Review how your current technical documentation can be assessed against the Saudi submission path.

items.title: Managing a product change
items.text: Clarify the documentation and planning questions to address before progressing a change or renewal.

support.title: Where we can support your submission programme
support.subtitle: The exact path depends on your product and its classification. We scope the work against your current evidence, the intended Saudi pathway and the practical steps required to proceed.

items.title: Pathway scoping
items.text: Clarify the product, intended use, classification context and key regulatory questions for Saudi market entry.

items.title: Technical-file gap assessment
items.text: Review available technical documentation and identify the information that needs attention before submission preparation.

items.title: Authorised Representative coordination
items.text: Coordinate the local representation and manufacturer documentation needed for the selected pathway.

items.title: MDMA and GHAD preparation
items.text: Prepare and organise the submission package and support the required portal workflow.

items.title: Lifecycle planning
items.text: Plan for updates, renewals and post-market obligations that may apply after market access.

process.title: What an MDMA readiness assessment covers
process.subtitle: Our initial review is designed to create an actionable next-step plan, not to promise an outcome before the product and evidence are understood.

items.title: Product and market context
items.text: We review the device, intended use, manufacturer status and commercial objective in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Existing evidence
items.text: We identify the approvals, quality-system information, clinical or performance evidence and technical-file materials already available.

items.title: Submission-readiness gaps
items.text: We map priority information and documentation questions to resolve before the MDMA preparation stage.

items.title: Recommended next steps
items.text: You receive a structured view of the likely workstreams, dependencies and questions to confirm with the relevant stakeholders.

items.question: What is an MDMA?
items.answer: MDMA refers to Medical Device Marketing Authorization. The applicable route and documentation depend on the device and its regulatory context.

items.question: Do foreign manufacturers need local representation?
items.answer: Local representation requirements and responsibilities need to be assessed for the manufacturer and selected pathway. We can help clarify the practical coordination required.

items.question: Can existing FDA, Health Canada or CE documentation be used?
items.answer: Existing evidence can inform the assessment, but it should be reviewed against the Saudi pathway and current product documentation before assumptions are made.

items.question: When should we start?
items.answer: Start before a commercial launch date is fixed. An early readiness review helps surface documentation dependencies and local coordination needs in time.

sfdaMdma.disclaimer: This page provides general information, not legal or regulatory advice. SFDA requirements, classifications, timelines and evidence expectations must be confirmed for the specific device and submission route.

hero.title: Privacy & Data Protection
hero.subtitle: How HealthUnion Global collects, uses and protects the information you share with us.

privacy.intro: This notice explains how HealthUnion Global handles personal data collected through this website, including the information and documents you submit through our intake and contact forms. We design our practices to align with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Canada's PIPEDA and Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).

sections.title: Who we are
body: HealthUnion Global is a regulatory affairs consultancy supporting medical device and cosmetics manufacturers across the United States (FDA), Canada (Health Canada), Saudi Arabia (SFDA) and the wider GCC region.
We act as the data controller for the personal data collected through this website.

sections.title: Information we collect
body: We only collect what we need to respond to your request and deliver our services:
items: Details you provide through our forms: company name, contact details, product category, device classification, target markets and your message.
Regulatory documents (PDF) that you choose to upload.
Your language preference and basic technical data required to operate the site securely.
We do not use advertising cookies or third-party tracking.

sections.title: How we use your information
body: We use your data to respond to your enquiry and prepare a pre-diagnostic of your regulatory pathway, to provide and manage our consulting services, to communicate with you, and to meet our legal and regulatory obligations.

sections.title: Legal bases for processing
body: Depending on your location, we rely on your consent, the performance of a contract or pre-contractual steps taken at your request, and our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries.
Where the GDPR, PIPEDA or PDPL apply, we process your data in line with the rights and obligations they set out.

sections.title: Storage and security
body: Form submissions are kept in a managed database. Documents you upload are stored in encrypted object storage and are served only through authenticated requests, never through public links.
Access is limited to authorised personnel, and we apply technical and organisational measures to protect your data.

sections.title: International transfers
body: Because we operate across borders, with teams in Canada and Riyadh, your data may be processed in a country other than your own. When we transfer data internationally, we apply appropriate safeguards consistent with applicable law.

sections.title: Data retention
body: We keep your personal data only for as long as necessary to respond to your request, deliver our services and meet our legal obligations. After that, we delete or anonymise it.

sections.title: Sharing your information
body: We do not sell your data and we do not share it for advertising. We may share it with trusted service providers who help us operate this site (for example hosting and email delivery) under appropriate confidentiality commitments, and with authorities where the law requires it.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Subject to applicable law, you may request access to your data, as well as its correction, deletion, restriction or portability, and you may object to certain processing. You may also withdraw consent at any time.

sections.title: Cookies
body: We use only essential cookies needed to operate the site and to remember your language and cookie preferences. We do not run advertising or analytics tracking at this time; if we introduce analytics in the future, we will ask for your consent first.

sections.title: Changes to this notice
body: We may update this notice from time to time. The "last updated" date above reflects the most recent version.

privacy.requestBody: For any question about this notice, or to exercise your rights, contact us through our contact page or by email. We respond to legitimate requests in line with applicable law.

sections.title: Information on this website

sections.title: No regulatory or legal advice
body: Website content does not constitute legal, regulatory, clinical or other professional advice. A device-specific assessment requires review of the product, evidence and intended market.

sections.title: Professional services
body: Any professional services are subject to a separate written agreement that defines the scope, responsibilities, fees, confidentiality and other applicable terms.

sections.title: Acceptable use
body: Do not interfere with the operation or security of this website, attempt unauthorised access, or use the website in a way that is unlawful or harms others.

sections.title: Third-party links
